Package com.datastax.oss.driver.api.querybuilder.insert

Interface InsertInto

  • All Superinterfaces:
    OngoingValues
    public interface InsertInto
extends OngoingValues
    The beginning of an INSERT statement; at this point only the table is known, it might become a JSON insert or a regular one, depending on which method is called next.

      • json

        @NonNull
default JsonInsert json​(@NonNull
                        Object value,
                        @NonNull
                        com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.type.codec.registry.CodecRegistry codecRegistry)
        Makes this statement an INSERT JSON with a custom type mapping. The provided Object value will be mapped to a JSON string.

        This is an alternative to json(String) for custom type mappings. The provided registry should contain a codec that can format the value. Typically, this will be your session's registry, which is accessible via session.getContext().getCodecRegistry().

        Throws:
        com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.type.codec.CodecNotFoundException - if codecRegistry does not contain any codec that can handle value.
        See Also:
        AttachmentPoint.getCodecRegistry()

      • json

        @NonNull
<T> JsonInsert json​(@NonNull
                    T value,
                    @NonNull
                    com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.type.codec.TypeCodec<T> codec)
        Makes this statement an INSERT JSON with a custom type mapping. The provided Object value will be mapped to a JSON string. The value will be turned into a string with TypeCodec.format(Object), and inlined in the query.
